info.title: Lodestar API
info.description: Every node is a new discovery. The JSON API under `/api/v1` (architecture §9): errors are always the `Error` envelope, and every path but the auth ones and this document needs the session cookie.

post.summary:
Marks alerts read up to `through` (the highest alert id you saw), for
one saved search or all of them. Alerts that arrived since stay unread.
It returns no count: one would reveal alerts that are withheld.

Unread alerts across every saved search, on torrents search would show:
the nav badge, equal to the sum of the saved searches' `unread`.
Whether the instance is set up and the caller logged in.

The trusted reverse-proxy header settings (§12). `forced_off` says
`LODESTAR_PROXY_AUTH=off` turned them off for this run.

Changes the trusted reverse-proxy header settings. Needs the password

get.summary:
Your classification rules, and how detection compares with your
corrections.

post.summary:
Your classification correction for one stored torrent; it's
classified again at once.

Adds a classification rule; the stored torrents it matches are
classified again. At most 1,000 rules: past that, 422
`too_many_class_rules`.

Removes a classification rule; the torrents it matched are classified
again without it.

Every collection, most recently changed first, with the number of
entries search would show.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Count torrents a filter rule hid too (§20.3).

post.summary: Makes a collection.

422.description: `invalid_value`: the name or note isn't allowed.

get.summary:
A collection and a page of its entries in order. Entries search
wouldn't show are skipped (a page is full unless the collection ends)
and `items` counts the ones it would.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The previous response's `next_after`: how many shown entries to
skip.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

delete.summary: Deletes a collection (not the torrents in it).

patch.summary:
Renames a collection or changes its note; absent leaves a field as it
is, and `note: null` removes the note.

422.description: `invalid_value`: the name or note isn't allowed.

post.summary:
Adds torrents to the end of a collection; ones already in it stay
where they are. All or nothing: a hash that is unknown, or that search
wouldn't show, is the one `404 torrent_not_found` (`field: "hashes"`)
and nothing is added.

Takes torrents out of a collection. A hash that isn't in it, is
unknown or isn't shown is skipped, so nothing about a withheld
torrent is revealed.

put.summary:
Puts a collection's entries in the order given. The list must name
every entry shown by default once (it may also name ones a filter rule
hid), with no cap, and may be empty only when none is shown;
`409 stale_order` otherwise, so a reorder from an old page can't
drop or duplicate entries. Entries not shown to the client (Adult while
hidden, and filter-hidden ones it did not name) keep their slots.

409.description: `stale_order`: the list isn't exactly the entries.

post.summary:
2–5 torrents side by side (§10.6): each one's summary and parsed
attributes, which attributes differ, the composition's shared scale
and the file lists compared by path and size.
post.description:
A hash that's unknown, hidden by a filter rule, or Adult while Adult
is hidden is the same 404 `torrent_not_found`, which names nothing.

get.summary:
The crawler: running or paused (and since when), its intensity, the
DHT node and the fetch pool.

patch.summary:
Sets the crawler's intensity at once: the same setting as
`crawler.intensity` in `/settings/crawler`, refused the same way when
an environment variable sets it.

post.summary:
Pauses harvesting and metadata fetching. The DHT node keeps answering
other nodes, fetches in flight finish, and indexing goes on. The
pause survives a restart. Pausing a paused crawler changes nothing.
Resumes harvesting and fetching where they stopped.

get.summary:
Discover (§10.7): the newest searchable torrents, paged like search
and optionally one content type's; the top torrents by swarm trend;
and ambiguous torrents just identified. A section this build can't
serve is `unavailable` with its reason, never an empty list.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The Newest tab: a content type (`movie`, `tv`, `music`,
`audiobook`, `ebook`, `comic`, `software`, `game`, `images`,
`video`, `other`, `adult`); absent is every type.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Newest rows per page: 1–200, 50 by default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The previous response's `newest.next_cursor`; send the same `type`
with it. It pages Newest only.

get.summary: The live event stream.
get.description:
Each frame is `id: <epoch>-<seq>` (none on `resync`), `event: <name>`
and `data: <json>`, the payload of the `Event` variant of that name.
Send the last id back as `Last-Event-ID` (`EventSource` does) to
replay what was missed; when that can't be done exactly (a restart,
too long ago, or an id that isn't ours), a `resync` comes first. A
client that falls behind gets a `resync` and carries on from live. A
comment every 15 s keeps the connection open; `retry:` is 5 s.

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description:
Comma-separated topics, e.g. `torrents,crawler`; all of them when
absent. An unknown or empty one is a 400 with `field: "topics"`.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last `id:` received, to resume after it.

200.description: The stream: one `Event` per frame (`event:` names the variant, `data:` holds its payload).

X-Accel-Buffering.description: `no`, so a proxy doesn't buffer it.

429.description: Too many open streams, in all or for this session (`too_many_streams`).

503.description: Not served here, or shutting down (`events_unavailable`).

get.summary:
Downloads a query's results as a file. To export an AST or a
selection of hashes, POST.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text, as `/search` takes it; empty (or no source at all) exports everything.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Export a collection instead, in its order.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: A comma-separated subset of `ExportField`; every field but `magnet` by default.

200.description: The file, streamed. Its job's id is in `X-Export-Job`; poll `/jobs/{id}` for progress, `skipped` and `truncated`.

400.description: A bad parameter, as `/search`'s, or `one_source`, `unknown_field`, `fields_unused`, `sort_unused`; `ast` or `hashes` in the query string is a `bad_parameter` (POST them).

429.description: `too_many_jobs`: four jobs are running or paused.

503.description: `search_disabled` (a query while search is off), or `shutting_down`.

post.summary:
Downloads a query's results (text or AST), a selection of up to
10,000 hashes, or a collection as a file.

parameters.name: hidden

get.summary:
A saved search's alerts as RSS 2.0: the 50 newest on torrents search
would show, each with a magnet enclosure. Feed readers that can't sign
in pass a feed token as `?token=`; an API key with the `feeds` scope
works too. Private-source torrents never appear. Anything the caller
can't have (another search's token, a search without RSS, an unknown
id) is the same `404 feed_not_found`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
A feed token (`lsf_…`), for feed readers that can't sign in. A
session or an API key with the `feeds` scope also works.

403.description: `key_scope`: an API key without the `feeds` scope.

get.summary: The rule set, switches and lists.

Applies a change. A change that weakens filtering is refused with 428
(`confirm_required`, the assessment beside the error) until it's sent
again with the admin password, every time (§20.11).

get.summary: The core rules' hashed examples, run against the rules as they are.

post.summary:
What a change would do, without applying it or asking for the
password.
Starts a preview in the background; poll it by its id.

A preview job: progress while it runs, then the assessment (or the
error) once it's done.

get.summary:
The review queue: quarantine (never with names) and the last 30 days'
decisions per rule.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Quarantine rows per page: 1–1000, 1000 by default.

post.summary:
How strict a candidate set of lists is (§2.9, §20.13): what it
would block and a warning matched to it. Nothing is stored or
connected.

Tries a draft rule and the current rules on example torrents. Nothing
is stored or logged.

get.summary:
Tombstones (dropped torrents) by hash and rule, never with names, in
pages; `adult=true` lists only adult holds.

parameters.name: adult
parameters.description:
Only adult holds: torrents held because you relabelled them adult,
which the 30-day purge left as tombstones.

get.summary:
Trend annotations (`restart`, `stopped`, `paused`, `resumed`,
`intensity`; other events are skipped) and the paused spans
overlapping `from..to`, so the client draws gaps.

The Insights overview (§10.9.2): stage strip, KPIs, trend with
annotations, the cohort funnel, segments, exceptions and Serve, from
the rollups. `compare=1` adds `previous` and `kpi.searchable_delta`.
Event time for the trend, new searchable, stages and Serve; discovery
cohort for the funnel, yield and time to searchable.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Unix seconds; `custom` only. Rounded down to its UTC hour (day,
for ranges over 7 days).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
Unix seconds, exclusive; `custom` only. Rounded up to its UTC hour
(day), and to the current one at most.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description:
`1` adds `previous`, the period of equal length before, and
`kpi.searchable_delta`.

get.summary:
Every job kept: running and paused ones, and those finished in the
last 10 minutes, newest first.
One job.

404.description: `job_not_found`: unknown, or finished more than 10 minutes ago.

post.summary:
Cancels a job: it stops at its next step (a paused one at once). A
cancelled export's download ends with an error, so it's never taken
for a complete file.

Pauses a job: it stops at its next step and holds nothing while it
waits (an export's download waits too). Unless it's resumed within
10 minutes it fails with `pause_expired`. Pausing a paused job does
nothing.
Resumes a paused job. Resuming a running job does nothing.

get.summary: Every API key and feed token, oldest first: never a secret.

post.summary:
Makes an API key or feed token. Needs the password (428
`confirm_required` without it). The secret is in this response only.

delete.summary: Deletes a key or token and its hash.

post.summary:
Replaces a key's secret: the old one stops working at once. The key
keeps its name, kind, scopes, feed and expiry, under a new id and
prefix. Needs the password (428 `confirm_required` without it).

Revokes a key or token: it stops working and stays listed as revoked.
Revoking one already revoked changes nothing.
Logs in; rate-limited per address.

200.description: Logged in; the session cookie is set.

post.summary: Clears the session cookie. The body is ignored but must be JSON.

get.summary:
Every log event (id, component, level, label and help keys, default,
current, data kinds, required, rate per hour), every data kind with its
switch per output and its deadline, the presets and the outputs. Admin
session only.

The network check: our address as other DHT nodes see it, and
whether unsolicited inbound queries reach the DHT port.

post.summary:
Starts the reachability measurement again (after changing a port
forward, say). At most once every 30 s (`429 rate_limited`).

get.summary: This document.

Parses a query: the AST and its canonical text, or a `query_syntax`
error whose `start`/`end` span the UI highlights. With
`natural=true`, also the query `q` means as natural phrasing
(`natural_too_long` past 512 bytes or 32 words).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text; empty matches everything.

parameters.name: natural
parameters.description:
Also read `q` as natural phrasing ("4k movies from 2020 over
10gb") and propose the query it means, in `natural`.

200.description: Changed; a new session cookie is set.

get.summary: Every saved search, oldest first, with its alert counts.

422.description: `invalid_value`: the name or query isn't allowed.

get.summary: One saved search.

delete.summary: Deletes a saved search with its alerts and feed tokens.

patch.summary:
Changes a saved search. Any subset: a field not sent keeps its value,
the notifier's channels included. Resuming a paused search skips what
was indexed while it was paused; editing the query does not move
where it left off.

422.description: `invalid_value`: the name or query isn't allowed.

get.summary:
A saved search's alerts, newest first. Only alerts on torrents search
would show: none a filter rule hid, and Adult only while "Show adult
content" is on. A page is full unless the list ends: withheld rows are
skipped, never counted.

400.description: `bad_cursor`: a cursor this server didn't give out.

get.summary: Searches with query text. To search with an AST, POST it.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text; empty browses everything.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `relevance` (the default), or `discovered`, `size` or `files` with an optional `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending, the default).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: `offset + limit` may not pass 10,000. Not with `cursor`.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `next_cursor`; send the same `q`, `sort` and `hidden` with it. An expired one is a 410 `cursor_expired`, a tampered one a 400 `bad_cursor`.

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: `1` or `true`: count every match exactly, within a time budget.

parameters.name: explain
parameters.description: `1` or `true`: explain each hit's score (`explain` in the response). First page only, at most 100 hits.

post.summary:
Searches with query text or a query AST. The body also takes
`"explain": true` (as `GET`'s `explain`).

Signs out every other browser: rotates the session key and sets a new
cookie for this one. Needs the password (428 `confirm_required`
without it).

200.description: Every other session ended; a new session cookie is set.

get.summary:
Every settings section, with the fields and JSON schema its form is
generated from.
get.description:
Each property of a section's schema carries hints for the form (the
server checks everything regardless): `x-group` (the group's id; its
heading is the message `settings.group.<id>`), `x-order`, `x-advanced`,
`x-preview` (`POST /settings/preview` has estimates or warnings for
it) and, where they apply, `x-unit` (`seconds`, `mebibytes`,
`connections`), `x-widget` (`radio`, `slider`, `theme`, `shortcuts`,
`language`, `time-zone`), `x-auto` (the value that means "automatic"),
`x-keywords` (a message key of search synonyms), `x-danger`
(`disruptive`, `privacy`, `destructive`, `security`, §10.10.7),
`x-config` (the `config.toml` key), `x-env` (the `LODESTAR_*`
variable), `format` (`socket-addr`, `log-filter`) and `writeOnly`
(a secret, never sent back).

patch.summary:
Changes several sections at once (`{section: {field: value}}`), as a
screen showing fields from several sections saves them: every
section's patch is checked as `PATCH /settings/{section}` checks it,
then all are saved in one transaction. One refused field saves
nothing; the error names its `section` and `field`.

409.description: `read_only`, `set_by_environment`, or `stale_revision` with each stale section's `current` values.

get.summary:
The saved settings as a TOML file to keep or move to another install,
laid out by section (`[crawler]`), each key with its `config.toml`
key and environment variable in a comment. It holds only values saved
in the app: never a secret, a value an environment variable sets, or
filter, floor, pack or subscription state (§20 has its own export).
`preferences` is included only when asked.

post.summary:
Reads a file from `GET /settings/export` and reports what it would
change. Keys that aren't settings, read-only ones, secrets and ones an
environment variable sets are listed in `skipped` and left alone.
Unless `dry_run=true`, the changes are then saved as one batch with
`PATCH /settings`' checks: all or nothing.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Only report what the import would change (the diff); save nothing.

409.description: `stale_revision`: a section changed since the dry run's `revisions`.

422.description: `invalid_import` (not an export file), or a value `PATCH /settings` refuses (`invalid_setting`, `adult_confirmation_required`). Nothing is saved.

post.summary:
What `PATCH /settings` with the same body would do, without saving:
the same checks and refusals, then for each patched field whether it
applies now or after a restart, warnings, and estimates where the
section can make them (fetch sockets, the new address, memory).

Tests a download client with the values on screen, before they're
saved: logs in and asks its version. It goes through the integrations
SSRF guard (download clients may be on this machine or the LAN, never
on link-local, metadata or reserved addresses). Nothing is saved, and
the result never repeats the URL or a credential.

200.description: The test ran; `ok` says whether it passed.

422.description: `bad_body`: not a test this endpoint runs.

429.description: `tests_busy`: four tests are running already; try again shortly.

get.summary:
One section's effective values, where each comes from, which can't be
changed here or wait for a restart, and its revision.

patch.summary:
Changes some of a section's settings. Every field is checked first,
then all are saved together; live ones apply at once, and the rest
are listed in `restart_required`. A field an environment variable
sets is refused, naming the variable. With `if_revision`, a section
changed since is refused with its current values.

422.description: `invalid_setting`; `adult_confirmation_required`: turning on an adult setting without `"confirm_adult": true`. Nothing is saved.

post.summary:
Claims a fresh instance with the setup token from the logs and a new
password; logs in.

200.description: Set up; the session cookie is set.

get.summary:
Every source plugin of this build: kind, consent class, stored state,
priority and health.

patch.summary:
Enables or disables a source, or sets its priority. A priority
applies at once; enabling or disabling at the next start. Enabling a
`restricted` or `overlay` source needs `"consent"` naming its class
(`409 consent_required` otherwise). Agents, egress, purge and the
schedule arrive in v0.6 (`409 not_editable`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The source's id, as `GET /sources` lists it.

get.summary:
The global bar's summary: searchable and stored torrents, harvest
and fetch rates, queue depth, index lag, disk, uptime. Unmeasurable
values are null, never 0.

Suggestions for the token at the caret: field names, values with
counts, titles, smart chips and "did you mean". `replace` ranges are
in characters, so the client never tokenises the query again.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query text as typed so far.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: The caret, in characters from the start; the end by default.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3), as `/search`.

get.summary:
The build, this installation, the restart and any pending address
change: everything About, the Overview and General show. A value this
platform can't measure is null, never 0.

post.summary:
Keeps the new HTTP address: this process is serving on it, so the
request itself shows it's reachable (whatever `Host` says: a reverse
proxy may rewrite it). `409 no_address_change` unless one is awaiting
confirmation.

Goes back to the previous HTTP address now. Awaiting confirmation,
the previous value is saved again and the server restarts onto it
(`restarting`); awaiting the restart, the saved change is undone and
nothing restarts. `409 no_address_change` when there's no change.

Restarts Lodestar: a graceful shutdown (the queue, DHT state and last
commit are saved), then the same program again. It answers first;
poll `/healthz` until it's back. `409 restart_unavailable` where it
can't restart itself, with how to restart instead.

409.description: `restart_unavailable`: restart it the way it was started (the message says how).

404.description: `torrent_not_found`, or `adult_hidden`: an Adult torrent while "Show adult content" is off.

Your marked torrents, newest change first. Only torrents search would

parameters.name: favourite
parameters.description: Only torrents you marked as a favourite.

parameters.name: hidden_mark
parameters.description:
Only torrents you marked Hide (your own mark, not a filter
rule's).

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3), as in search.

get.summary: Every label in use with the number of visible torrents carrying it.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Count torrents a filter rule hid too (§20.3).

get.summary:
A torrent's marks, and the collections it is in. A torrent without
marks answers with all-false, empty marks; an unknown torrent, or one
withheld (Adult while hidden), is `404 torrent_not_found`.

delete.summary: Clears every mark on a torrent.

patch.summary:
Changes some marks: absent leaves one as it is, `note: null` removes
the note. Labels and the note are trimmed first (and CRLF becomes LF).
Returns the marks after, all-false when none are left.

422.description: `invalid_value`: a label or the note isn't allowed (`field` names which).

AddressChange.description: A pending HTTP-address change (§10.10.6's lockout protection).

deadline.description: Unix seconds when it reverts, while awaiting confirmation.

previous_url.description: Where the UI was before the change.

stored.description:
False when the pending change couldn't be stored: the protection
lasts only until the process ends, and the log has the error.

url.description: Where the UI is after it.

AddressOutcome.description: `POST /system/address/keep` and `/revert`: the change as it is now.

oneOf.description: Null once kept (or a revert before the restart undid it).

restarting.description:
The server restarts on the previous address once this answer has
gone out.

AlertRow.description: One alert: a torrent a saved search matched once it became searchable.

created_at.description: When it was recorded, Unix seconds.

id.description:
The alert's id, never reused. `POST /alerts/read` takes the
highest one you saw.

AlertsEvent.description:
`event: alerts`: a saved search matched torrents that just became
searchable. One event per saved search per percolation run; the
matches themselves come from `GET /saved-searches/{id}/alerts`. Only
torrents search would show count: none a filter rule hid, and no
Adult while "Show adult content" is off (§20.9). A run whose new
matches are all hidden sends no event.

alert.description: The highest new alert's id (shown ones only).

matched.description: New alerts on torrents you can see; at least 1.

max_id.description: The highest of their torrent ids.

notify.description:
The saved search alerts in the app (its `alert` flag): notify only
when true. Otherwise the event only refreshes counts.

items.description: Newest first: only alerts on torrents search would show.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last.

AlertsRead.description:
`POST /alerts/read`: marks alerts read up to the highest one you saw,
so alerts that arrived while the page was open stay unread (§10.8's
"New since …" divider).

saved_search.description: One saved search's alerts; every saved search's when absent.

through.description: The highest alert id you saw.

text.description:
The event's detail: the version for `restart`, the new level for
`intensity`; empty when there's none.

version.description: The rule set's version after the change.

Assessment.description: A change's assessment (§20.10, §20.11). Field order: see [`Preview`].

confirm.description:
The password is needed (every weakening change, and marking a list
as part of the locked floor).

floor_entries.description:
For a floor removal: the entries the warning counts, 40 hex digits
each. A removal settles at most 10,000 at a time, so a longer
pending list goes in batches. Send these back as `hashes` to
confirm the removal with the password.

oneOf.description: For a keyword override: the same entry as *Neutralize term*.

warning.description: The plain-language effect warning; null for a strengthening change.

oneOf.description: Matches everything (an empty query: browse).
A word, tokenized when compiled.
Inclusive bounds; null is open.
Inclusive bounds; null is open.
File extensions; matches any.
40 lowercase hex digits.
A keyword facet; matches any of the values.
Torrents with at least one file matching every clause of `of`.
A category's share of the files or bytes, inclusive percentages.

AstWhen.description:
One end of a date range: seconds before the search (`ago`), or a Unix
time (`at`).

setup_required.description:
No password yet: claim the instance with the setup token from the
logs.

BackgroundJob.description: One job (`GET /jobs/{id}`, and each entry of `GET /jobs`).

done.description: Items done: rows written, for an export.

eta_s.description:
Seconds left at the current rate; null while it isn't running,
before the first items, or when `total` is unknown.

finished_at.description: Unix seconds; null while it runs.

rate.description:
Items read per second (`done` and `skipped`), paused time left
out; null before the first items.

skipped.description:
Items left out: for an export, torrents it may not include
(withheld, private-source, deleted or unknown), counted without
saying which or why.

total_approx.description: `total` is an estimate (a query with more than 100,000 matches).

BackgroundJobKind.description:
What a job does. `import` is reserved for the importer framework
(§18.8): nothing starts one yet, but the Jobs view can render both.

BackgroundJobState.description:
Where a job is. `running` and `paused` hold one of the running
slots; the rest are finished and kept for 10 minutes.

commit.description: The full commit hash; null when the build didn't know it.

date.description:
Unix seconds: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, else the commit's date; null
when neither was known (never the time of the build, so builds
stay reproducible).

rustc.description: `rustc -V` of the compiler that built it.

ui_build_id.description:
The embedded UI's build id (SvelteKit's `_app/version.json`); null
when the binary embeds the stub page.

oneOf.description: A pack (`malware`) or one pack rule (`MW-2`).

unless.description: An empty string removes the clause.

oneOf.description: Report torrents as child-abuse material (§20.5.2).

A quarantined torrent a rule caught wrongly (§20.12): an exception
for that torrent and that rule only, a hashed must-not-match
fixture for a core rule, and a release.

Releases a quarantined or dropped torrent: fetched and processed
normally next time it's seen.

Confirms a quarantined torrent as abuse material: into CS-1, sealed
name deleted.
Accepts or discards a version the sanity gates held back.

Settles floor entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped
(owner's decision §2.7). They stay blocked until this: `remove`
takes them out of the floor, which weakens it; otherwise they stay
in it as ordinary CS-1b entries. `source` is a pending source's key
(`file:<path>`, `list:<id>`).

A removal confirmed with the password must name its entries: send
back the assessment's [`Assessment::floor_entries`], so the
password confirms what the warning listed. Keeping may leave
`hashes` out, which keeps what the assessment counted.

Change.description: One change to filtering (§20.7), tagged by `op`.

ChangeBody.description:
`POST /filters/preview`, `/filters/preview/jobs` and `/filters/apply`.
`Debug` shows whether a password was sent, never the password.

password.description:
The admin password, for a change that weakens filtering (§20.11);
ignored by previews.

ChangedSetting.description: One setting changed from its default, by name only.

source.description:
Where a setting's effective value comes from, lowest to highest:
the built-in default, `config.toml`, a change saved in the app, or a
`LODESTAR_*` environment variable.

CharRange.description:
A range of characters (Unicode scalar values) in the query, end
exclusive.

queued.description:
Stored torrents queued to be classified again; null without a
search index (only torrents arriving later are affected).

truncated.description:
More stored torrents matched than are queued at once (1,000,000):
the rest are classified again when next re-enriched.

query.description: Can't test `type:` or `adult:`: the rule decides them.

Classes.description:
`GET /classify`: your classification rules, and how detection
compares with your per-torrent corrections (§20.9).

position.description:
1-based place among the entries shown, so it never reveals how
many were left out.

CollectionPage.description: `GET /collections/{id}`: the collection and a page of its entries.

entries.description: In order, only torrents search would show.

next_after.description: Send as `after` for the next page; null on the last.

CollectionPatch.description: `PATCH /collections/{id}`: absent leaves a field as it is.

CollectionSummary.description: A collection. `items` counts the torrents search would show.

hashes.description: 2–5 distinct 40-character hex info hashes, in column order.

differs.description:
For each parsed attribute any torrent has (the release fields:
`title`, `year`, `res`, `vcodec`, `group`, …), whether the values
differ across the set. A torrent without the attribute counts as
a different value.

file_diff.description: The file lists compared by path and size.

scale_bytes.description:
The shared scale for the composition bars: the largest `size` of
the set, in bytes.

torrents.description: One per hash, in the request's order.

attributes.description:
Every attribute in `differs`: this torrent's value, or null when
it has none. Lists are comma-joined.

composition.description: As in a search hit; empty before classification.

content_type.description: As in a search hit; null = not classified.

title.description: The effective title; null = not resolved.

CompositionShare.description: One colour group's share of a torrent (`docs/metrics.md` §4, §7.1).

bytes.description: Bytes in the group, padding excluded.

files.description: Files in the group, padding excluded.

pct_bytes.description:
Whole percent of the non-padding bytes: any non-zero share is at
least 1, and only a complete one is 100.

pct_files.description: The same, of the non-padding files.

ConfirmRequest.description:
`POST /sessions/revoke-others`, and any other change that only needs
the password (§20.11). `Debug` redacts it.

password.description:
The admin password, every time. Without it the answer is 428
`confirm_required`.

count.description:
How many are enabled (sources, lists, integrations); null for the
DHT, and for what this build doesn't have yet.

kind.description: Something Lodestar connects to (§10.10.13 "No telemetry, ever").

last_checked_at.description:
Unix seconds of the last contact, where it's recorded (a list's
last refresh).

settings.description: The Settings screen that changes it (`/settings/<screen>`).

state.description:
Null for what this build doesn't have yet (updates until the
update engine, companions and workers until v0.6).

Conversion.description: Each stage ÷ the one before, 0–1; null when the one before is 0.

floor.description: Part of the locked floor: can't be switched off.

CorrectBody.description:
`POST /classify/correct`: your correction to one stored torrent,
replacing any earlier one. `adult: null` and `not_junk: false` clear it.

held_by.description:
When relabelling it adult made filtering hold it back (§20.9): the
rule that did. It's then dropped or quarantined, no longer stored.

CrawlerEvent.description:
`event: crawler`: the same counters as the status page and
`/metrics`, sent every 5 s while anyone subscribes.

dht_nodes.description:
Nodes in the DHT routing table; null when the DHT is off or
hasn't reported yet.

harvested.description: Hashes received from sources since start.

paused.description:
The crawler is paused (`POST /crawler/pause`): the counters stand
still because nothing is harvested or fetched, not because
something broke.

CrawlerPatch.description:
`PATCH /crawler`: the global bar's intensity control. The same
setting as `crawler.intensity` in `/settings/crawler`.

intensity.description: How hard the crawler works (§5), as `/settings/crawler` has it.

CrawlerStatus.description: `GET /crawler`, and the answer to every crawler control.

oneOf.description: Null when the DHT is off or hasn't started yet.

intensity.description: How hard the crawler works (§5), as `/settings/crawler` has it.

intensity_env.description:
The environment variable that sets the intensity, which then
can't be changed here; null when it can.

since.description:
Unix seconds of the last pause or resume; the start when running
since then.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds, in the future; absent: never expires.

saved_search_id.description:
A feed token's saved search; absent: every feed. API keys take
none.

scopes.description:
An API key's scopes, at least one. A feed token takes none (it
reads feeds only).

CreatedKey.description:
`POST /keys` and `POST /keys/{id}/regenerate`: the key and, this once,
its secret. `Debug` redacts the secret.

secret.description:
The whole secret (`lsk_…` or `lsf_…`). Shown only now: Lodestar
keeps its hash, not the secret.

DataFormats.description: The data formats a bug report needs, and why an upgrade might reindex.

oneOf.description: A background index rebuild's progress; null when none runs.

store_schema.description:
The store's schema version (the last migration applied); null if
the store couldn't be read.

DataInfo.description: The data directory and what it holds.

cold_bytes.description: Bytes in the cold store; null when there is none.

database_bytes.description: Bytes in the database, its WAL and shared memory.

filesystem_warning.description:
What's wrong with its filesystem and the safe alternative (FUSE,
a network share, Unraid's user share); null when nothing is.

index_bytes.description: Bytes in the search index, every version included.

logs_bytes.description: Bytes in the log files; null when nothing is logged to files.

shadow.description: Decided in shadow mode: recorded, not acted on.

image_digest.description: The image's digest, when the image sets it.

image_tag.description: The image's tag, when the image sets it.

checked.description: Corrections that say adult or not.

disagree.description: Of those, ones detection gets wrong.

bootstrapped.description: It has a routing table to crawl from.

Diagnostics.description: The copyable diagnostics block's server half: never a value.

changed.description: Settings that aren't at their default, and where each comes from.

logging.description: The logging preset; null until file logging lands.

recent_errors.description: Errors logged recently; null until file logging lands.

newest.description: The newest searchable torrents, newest first.

rising.description: The top torrents by swarm trend.

DownloadClientDraft.description: A download client's settings as the form has them, unsaved.

password.description:
The password (qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission and rTorrent with
authentication) or the RPC secret (Aria2).

url.description: The client's address, as the form has it.

username.description:
The user name (qBittorrent; Transmission and rTorrent with
authentication).

DownloadClientKind.description: A download client a connection test can reach.

code.description: A stable snake_case identifier to branch on.

end.description:
The end of the fault's byte span within `field` (query syntax
errors).

field.description: The request parameter or body field at fault (`sort`, `ast.field`).

start.description: The start of the fault's byte span within `field`.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
`{ "error": { … } }`, plus the rare top-level key a client needs to
recover.

assessment.description:
On a 428 from `POST /filters/apply`: the warning to show before
asking for the password.

setup_required.description: On a 401: whether the instance still needs its first-run setup.

Event.description:
One frame of the stream: `event:` names the variant and `data:` holds
its payload. Every event but `resync` has an `id:` of the form
`<epoch>-<seq>` to send back as `Last-Event-ID`.

paused.description:
The paused spans overlapping the range, oldest first, so the
client draws gaps.

truncated.description: More than 1,000 annotations: the oldest 1,000 are listed.

phase1.description:
BM25 over the name and paths (`text`), fielded words and
filters; null under a field sort.

oneOf.description: Null under a field sort.

score.description: The score the hit was ranked by, as in `hits[].score`.

exact_name.description: Exact-name bonus: not ranked yet, always null.

file_cap.description:
The cap on file-only matches' contribution: not ranked yet,
always null.

name.description: The unfielded words' name boosts, summed (0 without phase 2).

phrase.description: Phrase and proximity bonus: not ranked yet, always null.

title.description: The unfielded words' parsed-title boosts, summed.

ExplainPriors.description:
The quality priors (§8), multiplied onto relevance once ranking has
them (with swarm health, M4); until then each is null.

ExplainWeights.description: The ranking's weights, as this server runs them.

name.description:
Boost of a word found in the name, in phase 1 (on the combined
field) and phase 2.

path.description: Boost of a word found in a file or folder name, in phase 1.

stem_score.description:
Phase-1 score of a word matched only by its stem in the title
(the plurals fallback, when `stemmed`).

title.description: Phase-2 boost of a word found in the parsed title.

ExportJob.description: What an export job reports besides its progress.

cap.description: Rows one export writes at most.

truncated.description:
The export stopped at `cap` with more rows left: the file holds
the first `cap`.

ExportRequest.description:
`GET /export`'s parameters and `POST /export`'s body. Name one
source: a query (`q` or `ast`, with `sort` and `hidden` as `/search`
takes them; neither exports everything), `hashes` or `collection`.
`ast` and `hashes` need POST.

oneOf.description: A query AST, as `/parse` returns it (POST only).

collection.description: A collection's id: its torrents in the collection's order.

fields.description:
A comma-separated subset of [`ExportField`] names, written in
that type's order whatever the order given. Every field but
`magnet` by default; `magnets` takes none.

oneOf.description: `csv` (the default), `json` (NDJSON) or `magnets`.

hashes.description:
Up to 10,000 info hashes (40 hex digits), such as the bulk bar's
selection (POST only). Repeats are exported once, in the order
first given.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

q.description: The query text, as `/search` takes it.

sort.description:
As `/search`'s; only with a query. Selections and collections
keep their own order.

ExternalAddress.description:
Our address as other DHT nodes see it: the BEP 42 `ip` key of their
replies, one vote per network (/24 or /64), the last 32 networks,
IPv4 and IPv6 tallied apart (the IPv4 consensus wins when both have
one).

agreeing.description: Voting networks naming the leading address.

ip.description:
The consensus address: at least 5 voters, and more than half of
them, agree; null until they do.

port.description: The port most of those voters saw; null without a consensus.

FacetsRequest.description:
`POST /facets`'s body. `GET /facets` takes the same fields as query
parameters, with `limit.<facet>=` for `limits` (and no `ast`).

oneOf.description: A query AST, as `/parse` returns it.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3), as `/search`.

lease.description:
A search response's `next_cursor`: count the same index snapshot
as its results. Send the same `q`, `sort` and `hidden` with it.
Without one, the index serving now.

limits.description: Values listed per facet: 8 by default, 1–100.

q.description:
The query text, as `/search` takes it. Send `q` or `ast`, not
both.

sort.description:
The search's sort; it doesn't change the counts, but a `lease`
is checked against it.

FacetsResponse.description:
`GET`/`POST /facets`. Counts are disjunctive: a facet's counts ignore
the query's own clauses on that facet (architecture §16, "B6").

backfill_before.description:
When the crawler first ran (Unix seconds); discovered bins that
end by then are `backfill`. Null when the store doesn't know.

buckets.description:
The swarm buckets: null until swarm health is in the index (M4),
never zeros.

canonical.description: The query as the server understood it.

facets.description:
Term facets by name: `type`, `ext`, `res`, `category`, `lang`,
`group`, `codec`, `audio`, `hdr`, `private`, `v2`, `has`,
`ambiguous`, `imported`, `backfill`, and `adult` when there are
adult subtypes to list.

sample_rate.description:
The share of the documents a sampled group visited (for the "≈"
note); null when nothing was sampled.

sampled.description:
Some group was computed on a sample (above 1,000,000 matches, or
300,000 when a segment holds more than 300,000 torrents).

total.description: The search's result count, as `/search` reports it.

unavailable.description:
Groups this index can't serve: fields an older index lacks while
it's rebuilt, and the swarm buckets until M4.

queued.description: Keys waiting for a fetch slot or for peers.

FieldPreview.description: One patched field, as it would be saved.

restart_required.description: It would apply at the next restart; otherwise at once.

value.description: The value it would have (null for a secret).

FileDiff.description:
The file lists compared: files match when their path (inside the
torrent, `/`-separated, decoded) and size are equal. Padding files
are left out.

common.description: Files every torrent has, in the first torrent's order.

only.description:
Per torrent, in the request's order: files no other torrent has.
With three or more torrents, a file some but not all have is in
neither list.

count.description: Files in the list in all, listed or not.

files.description: At most 2,000, in the torrent's order.

FilesPage.description: `GET /torrents/{hash}/files`: a page of the file list.

Fix.description: Where an exception's fix is: a settings section or a stage page.

failing.description: Examples the rule now gets wrong.

Fixtures.description:
`GET /filters/fixtures`: the core rules' hashed examples, run against
the rules as they are (§20.8).

FunnelCohort.description: One discovery cohort (or a UTC day of them) in the funnel (§10.9.3).

cohort.description: The cohort's first hour, unix seconds.

final.description:
Final: nothing in progress and everything stored searchable, or
past the 72 h retry horizon. A day is final when all its hours
are. Not final is "incomplete" (hatched).

losses.description:
Losses by reason (`no_peers`, `timed_out`, `refused`,
`encryption_failed`, `oversize`, `invalid`, `blocked`, `evicted`,
`gave_up`, `unreachable`), every reason listed.

FunnelStages.description: Hashes of the cohort that reached each stage.

FunnelTotal.description: The funnel over every cohort in the range.

cohorts.description: Cohort hours in the range with any count.

loss_share.description:
Each reason's share of all losses, 0–1; null when nothing was
lost.

HashList.description:
A list of torrents by info hash: `POST /collections/{id}/items`,
`…/items/remove` and `PUT …/order`.

Health.description: Health (§10.9.2): running, paused or degraded, with the reason.

Histogram.description: A histogram with explicit bins; empty bins are present with count 0.

missing.description:
Matches without a value (no year parsed); the bins plus this sum
to the result count.

unit.description:
What the edges measure: `bytes`; `hour`, `day`, `week` (from a
Thursday), `month` or `year` in UTC seconds (`discovered`, whose
first and last bins may be irregular edge bins); or `year` (the
release year).

backfill.description: Ends by the crawler's first run (`backfill_before`).

hi.description: Exclusive; null for the open top bin.

HitGroup.description:
A section of result rows (the row search returns) that may not be
available in this build or for this torrent. Unavailable is never an
empty list that reads as "none": `status` says which.

oneOf.description: Why it's unavailable; null when available.

truncated.description: More matched than the group lists.

cpus.description: CPU cores this process may use.

memory_bytes.description:
Memory this process may use: the machine's, or a container's
limit when lower.

from_source.description:
Where the value now comes from: to undo, send it back, or `null`
when this isn't `db`.

restart_required.description: It applies at the next restart.

ImportReport.description: `POST /settings/import`: the diff, and whether it was applied.

applied.description: Saved (false on a dry run, or when nothing changes).

revisions.description:
Every section's revision after the import: pass them back with
the real import to refuse it if anything changed after a dry run.

unchanged.description: Settings in the file that already have its value.

ImportSkip.description: A key in the file that an import leaves alone.

env.description: The variable that sets it, for `set_by_environment`; null otherwise.

key.description: `section.field`, or the key as the file has it.

InsightsEvent.description:
`event: insights` (reserved: B11a publishes it every 30 s): the stage
strip's headline numbers (`docs/metrics.md` §6.1, §7.5).

InsightsException.description: An exception (§10.9.2 level 5): text + icon + a fix action.

kind.description:
`index_lag` (the index more than 30 s behind) or `cohort_stalled`
(hashes in progress, the crawler running, and nothing stored for
2 full hours).

InsightsRange.description:
The range as the server normalized it: whole UTC hours, or whole UTC
days past 7 days.

to.description: Unix seconds, exclusive. The current hour (day) counts so far.

tz.description: The time zone buckets are in: always `UTC`.

JobStatus.description:
`GET /filters/preview/jobs/{id}`: progress while it runs, then the
assessment or the error.

error.description: Once `failed`: the error the preview would have returned.

KeyInfo.description: A key or token as listed: never its secret or hash.

last_used_at.description: Unix seconds, written at most once a minute; null: never used.

prefix.description: The secret's public start, to tell keys apart.

saved_search_id.description: A feed token's saved search; null: every feed (or an API key).

KeyScope.description: What a key may reach (see `keys::scope`). A route opts in to one.

imported.description:
Searchable torrents that were imported (bitmagnet import), part of
`searchable`; null until Insights' state is read at start.

new_searchable.description:
Torrents that first became searchable in the range, imports
included. Event time; 0 is real.

searchable.description: Documents in the search index now; null when search is off.

searchable_delta.description:
The change since the previous period's end: now's count less
`previous.kpi.searchable`. Null without `compare=1`, for `all`,
with search off, or with no snapshot from then.

time_to_searchable_p50_s.description:
First harvest → searchable, p50 and p95 seconds over the final
cohorts in the range. Always approximate (log buckets ≤ 10%).
Null when no cohort in the range is final.

yield.description:
Searchable ÷ harvested over the final cohorts in the range, 0–1.
Imports excluded. Null when no cohort in the range is final.

now.description: The server's clock (Unix seconds): deadlines are set from it.

LogComponent.description:
Where an event comes from (§12.1's per-component levels; `system` is
the process's own: start, stop, settings, logging).

LogDataKind.description:
A kind of data a line may contain (§12.1). `peer_activity` and
`filter_changes` are the opt-ins.

default_on.description:
On in the default preset (Normal). One that's off by default joins
at Detailed.

help_key.description: The message key of one line of help.

kinds.description: The data kinds it can carry (the badges).

label_key.description: The message key of its plain name ("Each failed metadata fetch").

oneOf.description: On only while this opt-in is.

rate_per_hour.description:
Lines per hour since start, from its counter, which counts while
it's off too.

LogKind.description: One data kind and its switch.

identifying.description: Identifies torrents or people: turning it on is time-limited.

opt_in.description:
Only by opt-in, for at most 24 hours, never by a preset, never on
the console or the Event Log.

until.description: When it turns off: 0 off, -1 until turned off, else Unix seconds.

LogKindOutputs.description: Whether a kind shows on each output.

LogLevel.description: A level, from the least to the most verbose.

LogOutputName.description: An output (§12.1): each has its own level and data kinds.

MatchInput.description:
What an override, exception or allow entry matches, as sent: exactly
one of the four.

NaturalChip.description: One recognised clause and the words it came from.

NaturalProposal.description:
What natural phrasing proposes (§10.4): recognised words become
clauses, and every other word stays as text.

canonical.description: The proposed query; it always parses back to `ast`.

chips.description: The recognised clauses, in the order they appear.

NetworkCheck.description:
`GET /network/check` and `POST /network/check`: the first-run
wizard's network check and the dashboard's "reachable" flag. Every
probe is ordinary DHT traffic; no outside service is asked (§18.7).

inbound_queries.description: DHT queries received in the window; null until measuring.

mapping.description: UPnP / NAT-PMP port mapping (§5). This build has neither.

min_window_s.description: `reachable` stays null until the window has run this long.

reachable.description:
Whether unsolicited inbound DHT queries arrive on the DHT port;
null is unknown.

unsolicited_queries.description: Of `inbound_queries`, the ones from nodes we hadn't sent anything to lately.

unsolicited_sources.description:
The distinct networks (/24 or /64) those came from, counting at
most the 64 most recent; null until measuring. `reachable` needs
at least 3.

window_s.description: The longest stretch of evidence looked at.

window_started_at.description:
Unix seconds the window started (bootstrap or a restart); null
before bootstrap.

NewestSection.description:
Discover's Newest: a page of result rows by `discovered_at`, newest
first, paged like search.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

notices.description:
As search's: `adult_hidden` for the `adult` tab while "Show adult
content" is off, so it's empty.

total.description: Searchable torrents in this tab, not just this page.

type.description: The tab; null is every type.

OkResponse.description: The body of a write that has nothing else to say.

scope.description: Applies only to what this query matches; null = everything.

Overview.description:
`GET /filters`: the rule set, switches and lists, as the Filters &
Safety screens show them.

pending_floor_removals.description:
Entries a config file or a floor-marked list dropped, still blocked
until you settle them (§2.7).

OverviewResponse.description:
The overview (§10.9.2): status, movement, the funnel, segments,
exceptions and Serve, for one range.

annotations.description:
Trend annotations in the range, oldest first, at most 1,000
(`/insights/events` says when there were more). Event time.

exceptions.description: What needs attention now, whatever the range (§10.9.2 level 5).

funnel.description:
The discovery cohorts in the range that have any count, oldest
first: hours up to 7 days, UTC days beyond (`range.bucket`).

funnel_total.description: The funnel over every cohort in the range.

ingest_per_hour.description:
Torrents newly stored in the last full UTC hour (§10.12). Event
time. Null when that hour wasn't measured (the crawler paused or
not running) and stored nothing.

previous.description:
The period of equal length just before, in the same shape;
present only with `compare=1`, and never for `all`.

oneOf.description:
Set when the rollups haven't been flushed for over 2 minutes
(§10.9.6); null when fresh.

trend.description:
Movement, one point per bucket (`range.bucket`), oldest first.
Event time.

updated_at.description: When the numbers were read (unix seconds).

ParseResponse.description: `GET /parse`: the AST and the canonical text it prints as.

natural.description:
With `natural=true`: the query `q` means as natural phrasing, for
the UI to preview as chips. Nothing applies it.

PasswordRequest.description:
`POST /password`: ends every other session.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

from.description:
Unix seconds: when it paused (before the range if it was already
paused then).

to.description: When it resumed; null while still paused.

PendingFloorEntry.description: Floor entries one source dropped, waiting for a decision (§2.7).

hashes.description: Up to 1,000 of them, 40 hex digits each.

name.description: The file's path, or the list's name.

Preview.description:
What a change would do (§20.10). Counts come from the review queue,
the tombstones, the filter hits of the replay window and the index.

Fields are in the order `POST /filters/preview` has always sent them;
where an assessment is nested in another body, its keys are sorted.

caught_30d.description: Decisions in the replay window by the rules it affects.

core_caught_30d.description: Of those, by the child-safety core.

estimate.description:
Counts from names only (sealed names, no file lists), so files'
evidence isn't re-checked: treat as an estimate.

quarantine.description: Quarantined items it would release now.

removed_from_floor.description: Entries that would leave the locked floor.

stored.description: Stored items whose hide, demote or flag mark it would clear.

tombstones.description: Dropped items it would let be fetched again.

PreviewEstimate.description: A consequence the preview can put a number on, for the UI to format.

name.description:
What it measures: `sockets` (concurrent metadata fetches), `url`
(where the UI will be after a restart), `memory_mib`.

PreviewWarning.description: Something worth knowing before saving; it doesn't stop the save.

example.message: Search stops after the restart, until you turn it back on.

PreviousKpi.description: The KPIs over the previous period.

searchable.description:
Searchable at the period's end: the last hourly snapshot in the
day before it ends. Null when there's none (search off, or not
running then).

PreviousPeriod.description: The previous period, for Compare: the fields that depend on the range.

PreviousStages.description: The stage strip over the previous period.

allowed_users.description: Empty: any user the proxy names.

forced_off.description:
`LODESTAR_PROXY_AUTH=off` turned proxy auth off for this run; the
saved settings shown here don't apply until it's removed.

header.description: The header the proxy names the signed-in user in.

trusted.description: The proxies whose header is believed, as canonical CIDRs.

allowed_users.description: At most 64 user names; empty allows any.

trusted.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges, at most 64. Required to turn it on.

adult_hold.description:
Held only because you relabelled it adult (a correction or a
classification rule) and the Adult-only core caught it: at
`expires_at` it becomes a tombstone rather than being released.

expires_at.description: When its sealed name is deleted and its quarantine ends.

Queue.description:
`GET /filters/queue`: quarantine (never with names) and the replay
window's decisions per rule.

next_cursor.description: The next page of quarantine, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

RebuildEvent.description:
`event: rebuild`: index rebuild progress (§8, the "Index rebuilding"
banner of §10.4), sent when it changes, and once more with `done`.

done.description: Torrents in the new index so far.

unavailable.description: Fields that match nothing until the swap.

RebuildPhase.description: A rebuild's phase; `done` once the new index serves.

RestartAccepted.description:
`POST /system/restart`: accepted; the server restarts once this
answer has gone out.

estimated_seconds.description: About how long until it answers again.

Seconds this run took from start to listening: about how long a
restart pauses crawling.

hint.description: When it isn't available, how to restart instead.

ResyncEvent.description:
`event: resync`: events were missed; refetch what the page shows, then
carry on with the events that follow. It has no `id:`.

action.description: Null for an action code this server doesn't know.

shadow_until.description: Shadow mode ends then: until then it only records what it would do.

Sample.description: One example torrent for `POST /filters/test`, never stored or logged.

type.description: A content type (`movie`, `adult`, …), replacing the classifier's.

SampleFile.description: A sample's file: a path, or a path and its size.

alert.description: Alert in the app about new hits.

oneOf.description: A query AST, as `/parse` returns it.

q.description:
The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both; with neither it
matches everything.

rss.description: Serve the hits as an RSS feed.

SavedSearchPatch.description:
`PATCH /saved-searches/{id}`: any subset; absent leaves a field as it
is (the notifier's channels too).

paused.description:
Pausing and resuming is a toggle; resuming skips what was
indexed meanwhile.

SavedSearchView.description:
A saved search with what the list view shows beside it. The
notifier's channels and the watermark are not part of it.

alert.description: Alert in the app about new hits.

last_alert_at.description: When the newest alert was recorded; null before the first.

paused.description: Skipped by the notifier; its channels are kept.

rss.description: Serve the hits as an RSS feed.

sort.description: The sort the results open with; null = relevance.

SearchExplain.description:
How a first page was ranked (`?explain=1`, architecture §8). Field
names are stable. Relevance is `phase1 + phase2.name + phase2.title`
(to float rounding); the other features and the priors aren't part of
ranking yet and are null.

hits.description: One per hit, in the hits' order.

ranked_by.description:
`relevance`, or the field the hits are sorted by (`discovered`,
`size`, `files`), when no hit has relevance parts.

two_phase.description:
Whether phase 2 re-ranked the phase-1 candidates: the query has
unfielded words.

SearchHit.description:
One search result: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1), its
relevance and, for a query with a file clause, the files that matched.

composition.description:
What the torrent is made of, by colour group, in the composition
bar's order; groups without files are left out, and it's empty
before classification.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

junk_reasons.description:
Stable reason keys (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1); empty when there are
none or before classification.

matched_files.description:
Positions in the torrent's file list; present only when the query
has a file clause.

resolved_via.description:
How the title was found when the name wasn't informative:
`files`, `folder` or `structure`; null = from the name itself, or
not classified.

title.description: The resolved title; null = not resolved.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

SearchNotice.description: A note on what a search left out.

SearchRequest.description:
`POST /search`'s body, and `GET /search`'s parameters (where `ast` is
refused: send an AST with POST).

oneOf.description:
A query AST, as `/parse` returns it; it must be one the parser
could produce.

cursor.description:
The previous page's `next_cursor`, to read the next page from the
same index snapshot. Send the same `q` (or `ast`), `sort` and
`hidden` with it.

exact.description:
Count every match exactly, even above 100,000 (within a time
budget; `total_approx` says whether it made it). `1` or `true`.

hidden.description: Include torrents a filter rule hid (§20.3).

offset.description: `offset + limit` may not pass 10,000. Not with `cursor`.

q.description: The query text. Send `q` or `ast`, not both.

sort.description:
`relevance` (the default), or `discovered`, `size` or `files` with
an optional `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending, the default).

canonical.description: The query as the server understood it.

explain.description: Present only when asked for with `explain`.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page, read from the same index
snapshot (§8); null on the last page. Opaque, URL-safe, at most
256 characters, valid for 10 minutes after its last use.

notices.description:
What the server left out of these results, for the UI to say:
`adult_hidden` when the query asks for Adult (`type:adult`,
`adult:…`) while "Show adult content" is off, so it matched
nothing adult (§20.9).

stemmed.description:
Few exact matches: plural forms in titles were included too (§8),
ranked after the exact ones.

total.description: Matches in all, not just this page.

total_approx.description:
`total` is an estimate (above 100,000 matches; shown with "≈");
ask with `exact` for the exact count.

restart_required.description:
Fields whose saved value differs from the running one: they take
effect at the next restart.

revision.description:
Goes up by one with every save that changes the section. Send it
back as `if_revision` to refuse a save over someone else's.

yield.description: Searchable ÷ harvested, 0–1; null when it harvested nothing.

Segments.description:
Segments (§10.9.2 level 4). Rows are sorted by value, descending, then
key. Adult is left out entirely while "Show adult content" is off.

by_content_type.description:
Newly searchable by content type (`movie`, `tv`, …, `adult`, and
`unclassified` for none yet). Event time.

by_group.description:
The same by the content type's group: `video` (movie, tv, video),
`audio` (music, audiobook), `documents` (ebook, comic),
`software` (software, game), `images`, `other`, `adult`,
`unclassified`. Event time.

by_source.description:
Yield by the source that found each hash first, over final
cohorts. Discovery cohort.

Serve.description:
Serve (§10.9.2 level 6). Every field is null until its counter exists:
searches and latency with #48, alerts with B9, sends with the
integrations' counters.

zero_result_rate.description: Searches that found nothing ÷ searches, 0–1; null with no searches.

SettingField.description: One field of a section, for its form.

env.description: The environment variable that overrides it; null when none does.

help_key.description: Message key of the help text beside the field.

label_key.description: Message key of the field's label.

read_only.description: Never editable in the app (e.g. the data directory).

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

SettingSource.description:
Where a setting's effective value comes from, lowest to highest:
the built-in default, `config.toml`, a change saved in the app, or a
`LODESTAR_*` environment variable.

env.description: The variable that set it when `source` is `env`; null otherwise.

read_only.description:
Can't be changed in the app: set by the environment, or never
editable here.

restart_required.description: A change takes effect at the next restart.

value.description: Any JSON value, of the type the section's schema gives the field.

SettingsBatch.description:
`PATCH /settings` and `POST /settings/preview`: patches for several
sections, `{section: {field: value}}`, each as `PATCH
/settings/{section}` takes it. Saved all together or not at all.

code.description: A stable snake_case identifier to branch on.

message.description: A sentence for people. It never repeats a secret's value.

SettingsErrorEnvelope.description:
A refused settings change: the API's error envelope, plus the
`section` at fault and, for `409 stale_revision`, the current values
of every section that changed meanwhile.

current.description:
On `409 stale_revision`: each stale section's values now, to merge
the edit with.

SettingsEvent.description:
`event: settings`: a section was saved (by any tab, device or API
client) and is now at `revision`. It carries no values: fetch them
with `GET /settings/{section}`.

confirm_adult.description:
The 18+ confirmation, needed when the file turns on an adult
setting (as `PATCH /settings/content` needs it).

revisions.description:
The sections' revisions the dry run reported: the import is refused
with `409 stale_revision` if any changed since.

toml.description: The file's text (TOML), at most 64 KiB.

SettingsPatch.description:
`PATCH /settings/{section}`: some of the section's fields and their
new values, as its schema in `GET /settings` describes. Fields left
out keep their values; an unknown field is refused. `null` resets a
field: its saved value is removed, and the `config.toml` value or the
default applies again.

Two keys aren't fields and are never saved: `if_revision` (the
section's `revision` the edit started from; a save over a newer one is
refused with `409 stale_revision`) and a section's confirmations
(`content`'s `confirm_adult`).

SettingsPreview.description:
`POST /settings/preview`: what a `PATCH /settings` with the same body
would do, without saving it.

SettingsSection.description: One section: its fields and the JSON schema of its values.

schema.description:
A JSON Schema (2020-12) object for the section's values, with
each number field's bounds as `minimum`/`maximum`.

allOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

oneOf.description: Log in to a download client and ask its version.

SettingsTest.description: `POST /settings/test`: what to test, with the values on screen.

message.description: A sentence for people; never the URL or a credential.

example.message: The client refused the user name or password.

SettingsTestResult.description:
`POST /settings/test`: the result, shown beside the button. Nothing is
saved either way.

api_version.description: The client's API version, when it has one apart from its version.

oneOf.description: Why it failed; null when `ok`.

version.description: The client's version, as it reports it; null unless `ok`.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /setup`: claims the instance.
`Debug` redacts the secrets.

token.description:
The one-time token printed to the logs (`XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, any
case).

SiblingsResponse.description:
`GET /torrents/{hash}/siblings`: the torrents related to one, in three
groups. Each is either available (possibly empty) or unavailable with
a reason.

hash.description: 40 hex digits: the torrent asked about.

identical_payload.description: Identical-payload clones: the same content under another hash.

oneOf.description:
What other versions were matched on; null when the torrent has no
parsed title.

other_versions.description:
Other versions of the same work (other releases, qualities,
groups), best first.

same_file.description: Other torrents containing one of this torrent's files.

Source.description: One source plugin of this build.

consent_required.description: Enabling it needs `"consent"` naming its class.

not_yet_editable.description:
Fields planned for the v0.6 sources epic (agents, egress, purge,
schedule): listed so the UI can show them, refused by `PATCH`.

priority.description: A source's share of the fetch pool (§18.4: weights 1 / 3 / 6 / 10).

restart_required.description:
Its stored state differs from what's running: it starts or stops
at the next restart.

harvested_24h.description: Keys it was first to report in the last 24 hours.

last_error.description: Why it last stopped with an error; null when it didn't.

last_run.description:
Unix seconds it last started; null when it hasn't run since the
process started.

SourcePatch.description:
`PATCH /sources/{id}`. Fields left out keep their values. A new
priority applies at once; enabling or disabling takes effect at the
next start (`restart_required`).

agents.description: Not editable before v0.6: refused with `409 not_editable`.

oneOf.description: What enabling a source requires (§18.7).

consent.description:
The consent class you agree to; needed to enable a source whose
class is `restricted` or `overlay`, and must be that class.

egress.description: Not editable before v0.6: refused with `409 not_editable`.

priority.description: A source's share of the fetch pool (§18.4: weights 1 / 3 / 6 / 10).

purge.description: Not editable before v0.6: refused with `409 not_editable`.

schedule.description: Not editable before v0.6: refused with `409 not_editable`.

discover.description:
Unique hashes harvested in the range (first harvests: the cohorts'
harvested counts). Always approximate (≈).

fetch.description:
Metadata retrieved in the range, by event time (the writer's
flush). Null when the range starts before fetches were counted by
event time (the first whole hour after the upgrade that added it):
unknown, not 0.

index.description: Searchable torrents now; null when search is off.

serve.description:
Searches answered in the range; null until search counters exist
(#48).

understand.description: Torrents newly stored in the range. Event time.

since.description: The last flush, or the start when there was none since.

StatsResponse.description:
`GET /stats`: what the global bar and status pill show
(`docs/metrics.md` §7.6).

data_bytes.description: Bytes the data directory holds (database, index, state).

disk_free_bytes.description:
Bytes free on the data directory's volume; null where this build
can't measure it.

fetched_per_hour.description:
Info dicts fetched per hour, over the last 5 minutes; null in the
first minute.

harvested_per_hour.description:
Keys the sources reported per hour, over the last 5 minutes; null
in the first minute.

index_lag_s.description:
Seconds the index trails the store's last commit; null when search
is off or either hasn't committed since the start.

queue_depth.description: Keys queued or in flight in the fetch pool.

searchable_torrents.description: Documents in the search index; null when search is off.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds these numbers were read.

Strictness.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: what the lists would block, and a warning
matched to it (§2.9, §20.13).

estimate.description:
Some figures are the catalog's measurements of lists not fetched
yet, and lists may overlap: a lower bound.

floor_hashes.description: Torrents a floor-marked list blocks by hash.

ipv4_public_share.description: The share of public IPv4 blocked (0–1); the level reads this.

ipv4_share.description: The share of all IPv4 blocked (0–1).

ipv6_share.description: The share of IPv6 global unicast blocked (0–1).

unknown.description: Lists never fetched, so what they block isn't known.

StrictnessBody.description:
`POST /filters/strictness`: a candidate set of lists to assess,
subscriptions by id and catalog lists by key (`lodestar lists`), in
any mix.

StrictnessList.description: One list's figures in a [`Strictness`]; null where unknown.

measured.description: The figures are a catalog measurement, not this list's data.

SuggestItem.description:
One suggestion: replace the query's characters `replace.start` to
`replace.end` (end exclusive) with `insert`. A leading `-` or `!`
stays outside the range.

count.description:
Torrents it would find, of those this search may show; absent for
field names, categories and "did you mean".

insert.description: The query text to put in.

text.description:
What to show: the value, title or field, or for `did_you_mean`
the whole corrected query.

items.description: "Did you mean" first, then chips, field names, values and titles.

SwarmBuckets.description:
Seeders and trackers reporting, as `≥1`, `≥5`, `≥50` and
`never_scraped` values (§10.4).

SwarmSample.description:
One day or week of swarm history. Counts saturate at 65,534; null is
a gap.

at.description:
The start of the UTC day, or of the week (epoch day / 7: weeks
start on Thursday).

oneOf.description: A pending HTTP-address change; null when there is none.

channel.description: The release channel this build came from. `dev` is a local build.

connections.description: Everything Lodestar connects to, each with its state.

fixture.description:
Serving a fixture's test data (`lodestar serve --fixture`), not a
real install.

repository.description:
The source repository (`Cargo.toml`'s `repository`), so a fork
links to itself.

restart_required.description: Saved settings that apply at the next restart, as `section.field`.

approx.description: Computed on a sample: show the counts with "≈".

distinct.description: Distinct values with a count, listed or not.

other.description:
The counts of the values not listed, summed (a torrent with two
such values counts twice).

values.description:
The top values by count (ties by value), then any value the query
selects or excludes that isn't among them. Flags list `yes` and
`no`.

TestBody.description: `POST /filters/test`: a draft rule and examples to try it on.

oneOf.description: What the current rules decide; null = nothing.

draft.description: Whether the draft matches; null without a draft.

shadow.description: Rules in shadow mode that would have decided.

TitleIdentity.description:
A work's title identity (`docs/decisions/2026-10-22-B13.md`): its normalized title plus the
year, season and episode spans the release names, if any.

title_words.description:
The title's words as search tokenizes them, lowercased and
folded.

adult_hold.description: Left by an adult hold's quarantine at the 30-day purge.

Tombstones.description:
`GET /filters/tombstones`: dropped torrents, by hash and rule (no
names), so one can be found and released.

next_cursor.description: The next page, if there is one: pass as `cursor`.

Topic.description: What a client subscribes to with `?topics=`.

TorrentDetail.description:
`GET /torrents/{hash}`: the torrent summary (`docs/metrics.md` §7.1),
its swarm section (§7.2) and the first 500 files.

The swarm fields are `null` until swarm health is served (M4): null is
"never scraped", never 0.

dht_peers.description: BEP 33 estimate of peers (always approximate); null = no estimate.

dht_seeds.description: BEP 33 estimate of seeds (always approximate); null = no estimate.

file_list.description: The first files, in the torrent's order; the rest via `/files`.

hash_v2.description: 64 hex digits; null for a v1-only torrent.

oneOf.description:
14 daily and 26 weekly samples, newest first; null = no history
kept.

swarm_trend.description:
Seeders per day over the last week; null = fewer than 3 daily
samples.

trackers_checked.description:
Trackers that answered in the last answered round; null = never
scraped.

trackers_reporting.description: Of those, trackers that reported anyone; null = never scraped.

TorrentsEvent.description:
`event: torrents`: torrents you can see became searchable. Commits
close together may arrive as one event. While "Show adult content" is
off, Adult torrents are left out entirely: not counted, and a commit
of only those sends no event.

added.description:
Torrents new to the index since the previous `torrents` event,
leaving out Adult while it's hidden; at least 1.

max_id.description:
The highest torrent id searchable now, while Adult is shown.
**Null while Adult is hidden:** ids are sequential, so any real id
sent beside an exact `added` would show, in its gap from the last
one, how many hidden torrents arrived. To find what's new, use the
newest id among your own results (or a cursor), not this.

TrendPoint.description:
One trend bucket. A count is null where nothing was measured (a gap:
paused, or not running), and 0 where it was measured and was 0.

harvested.description: Unique hashes first harvested in the bucket. Always ≈.

searchable.description: Torrents newly searchable in the bucket.

Unavailable.description: Why a section isn't available. Stable keys; the UI words them.

unread.description:
Unread alerts across every saved search, on torrents search would
show: the sum of the saved searches' `unread`.

UserItemDetail.description: `GET /user-items/{hash}`: the marks and the collections it is in.

collections.description: Ids of the collections the torrent is in ("In collections").

UserItemPatch.description:
`PATCH /user-items/{hash}`: what to change. Absent leaves a mark as
it is.

labels.description:
Replaces the labels (at most 32, 1–64 characters each); an empty
list removes them.

UserItemRow.description: One marked torrent: your marks and the torrent beside them.

UserMarks.description:
A torrent's marks. Without any, `favourite` and `hidden` are false,
`labels` is empty and the rest is null.

created_at.description: Null when there are no marks.

updated_at.description: Null when there are no marks.

Error.description: Any failure: the error envelope. `error.code` is stable; branch on it.

session.name: lodestar_session
session.description: The session cookie `/setup`, `/login` and `/password` set. HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict.

tags.name: crawler
tags.description: Stats, the crawler's controls, sources and the network check (§9, §10.9, §18.8).

tags.name: library
tags.description: Your marks, collections and saved searches (§7, §10.5, §10.8).

tags.name: logs
tags.description: What gets logged: events, data kinds and outputs (§12.1).

tags.name: export
tags.description: Search results, selections and collections as files (§9, §10.4).

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Background jobs: exports now, imports later (§9, §18.8).
